2023-09-25.headline: Entra ID sets 30 September 2025 deadline to leave legacy MFA and SSPR method management
2023-09-25.overview: The period’s only supplied update is a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update for Entra ID. Microsoft says it will retire the ability to manage authentication methods through the legacy Multifactor Authentication (MFA) and Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) policies on 30 September 2025. This is a forward-looking retirement notice, not evidence of an immediate behavior change this week.
2023-09-25.adminImpact: Administrators should plan to migrate methods managed through the legacy MFA and SSPR policies to the converged Authentication methods policy before the deadline. Microsoft describes that policy as the central management point for passwordless, multifactor authentication, and SSPR scenarios. The supplied notice does not include migration steps or technical prerequisites.

keyChanges.title: Management of methods in the legacy policies will be retired
keyChanges.detail: On 30 September 2025, Entra ID will no longer support managing authentication methods in the legacy MFA and SSPR policies. The notice specifically describes retirement of management in those policies; it does not say that the authentication methods themselves will be removed on that date.

2023-12-04.headline: Entra ID FIDO2 registration may offer passkey creation on another device
2023-12-04.overview: The week contains one Entra ID Message Center notice. It describes a changed FIDO2 security key registration experience in which users may receive an operating system- or browser-generated prompt to create a passkey on another device, such as a phone or tablet; some users may see a QR code for that flow. The notice does not establish a preview or general-availability milestone, a policy change, or a required administrator action.
2023-12-04.adminImpact: The concrete impact is to the user experience during FIDO2 registration. Administrators and support teams should be aware that a passkey-on-another-device prompt or QR code may be expected. The supplied evidence identifies no configuration change, migration, retirement, or mandatory action.

keyChanges.title: Alternate-device passkey prompts can appear during FIDO2 registration
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID users registering a FIDO2 security key may see a prompt generated by their operating system or browser to create a passkey on another device, including a phone or tablet. In some cases, a QR code facilitates the option. This is a registration-experience change, not evidence of a separate product launch or availability announcement.

2024-01-22.headline: India-specific removal of MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp is the only Entra ID change recorded
2024-01-22.overview: For the week of 22 January 2024, the supplied data records one Entra ID item: a 26 January Microsoft 365 Message Center notice about removing MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp in India. There are no recorded new, updated, or removed feature or documentation items, and the notice is a service-change communication rather than a feature launch or preview.
2024-01-22.adminImpact: Organizations without users in India can safely disregard the notice, according to its summary. Organizations with users in India should determine whether they rely on this delivery route. The supplied evidence does not state an effective date, replacement method, or specific migration task.

keyChanges.title: MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp is being removed in India
keyChanges.detail: The Entra ID Authentication notice describes a regional removal of this MFA delivery capability. It is an operational behavior change, not evidence of general availability, preview, or documentation clarification. No timing or replacement channel is provided in the supplied message.

2024-02-19.headline: Entra ID prepares a device-bound passkey preview, with FIDO2 policy and sign-in changes
2024-02-19.overview: The period’s sole supplied item is a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice about a substantive Entra ID authentication change, not a general-availability announcement or a documentation clarification. Beginning in mid-March 2024, Entra ID is expected to add preview support for device-bound passkeys stored on computers and mobile devices alongside existing FIDO2 security-key support. The rollout also changes FIDO2 policy handling and makes the end-user sign-in terminology cover passkeys from all supported device types.
2024-02-19.adminImpact: Administrators will need to enforce key restrictions in the FIDO2 policy to allow the passkey providers they intend to support. They should also expect the Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 sign-in option to use new, broader wording. The supplied notice does not state that existing FIDO2 security-key support is being retired or that a migration is required.

keyChanges.title: Device-bound passkeys enter Entra ID as a preview authentication method
keyChanges.detail: Starting in mid-March 2024, Entra ID will support device-bound passkeys stored on computers and mobile devices, in addition to its existing support for FIDO2 security keys. The notice identifies this as a preview; it does not establish general availability.

keyChanges.title: FIDO2 policy must permit the intended passkey providers
keyChanges.detail: To allow specified passkey providers, administrators will need to enforce key restrictions in the FIDO2 policy. This is the concrete configuration impact of extending supported credentials beyond security keys.

keyChanges.title: The Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 sign-in label becomes more inclusive
keyChanges.detail: The end-user option will be renamed to "Face, fingerprint, PIN, or security key." The updated sign-in experience will also use the term "passkey" so the wording covers passkey credentials presented from security keys, computers, and mobile devices.

2024-03-04.headline: Microsoft 365 Admin Center user-consent setting to be retired in early April
2024-03-04.overview: The only reported Entra ID change for the week is the retirement of the “User consent to Apps” setting in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center. This changes where the tenant-wide user consent policy is managed, not the existing policy itself.
2024-03-04.adminImpact: No preparation is required. Existing settings will remain unchanged, but administrators will no longer be able to view or edit the policy in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center after the retirement. Use the user consent settings in the Entra portal instead.

keyChanges.title: Retirement of the Microsoft 365 Admin Center consent setting
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft 365 Admin Center experience for “User consent to Apps” will be retired in early April 2024. Management of the tenant-wide user consent policy moves to the corresponding Entra portal experience; the change does not alter existing settings.

2024-03-11.headline: Entra ID: PIM enters Power Platform public preview while Copilot welcome emails expand to external license assignments
2024-03-11.overview: The week of 11 March 2024 contains two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices for Entra ID. One announces the public preview of Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in the Power Platform admin center, a capability already available since 5 February. The other describes an upcoming late-March through late-April rollout that will send Copilot for Microsoft 365 welcome emails when licenses are assigned through PowerShell or the Microsoft Entra admin center. These notices represent a public preview and a change in email behavior—not a reported general-availability release or retirement.
2024-03-11.adminImpact: Power Platform administrators should treat the PIM integration as preview functionality. Organizations that assign Copilot for Microsoft 365 licenses through PowerShell or the Microsoft Entra admin center can review direct-communication preferences ahead of the rollout. The notice says organizations can adjust preferences in the Microsoft 365 admin center, while individual users can change their own settings through security and privacy controls; it identifies no required migration.

keyChanges.title: Entra PIM is in public preview in the Power Platform admin center
keyChanges.detail: The 13 March notice announces public preview availability of Entra Privileged Identity Management within the Power Platform admin center; the capability was made available on 5 February 2024. Microsoft describes PIM as providing management, control, and monitoring of access to important organizational resources. The supplied notice does not claim general availability or specify additional requirements.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID / Power Platform admin center

keyChanges.title: Copilot welcome emails will cover licenses assigned outside the Microsoft 365 admin center
keyChanges.detail: PowerShell and the Microsoft Entra admin center will support Copilot for Microsoft 365 welcome emails when licenses are assigned through methods other than the Microsoft 365 admin center. The rollout is scheduled to begin in late March 2024 and finish in late April 2024. End users will automatically receive the email when direct communications from Microsoft are enabled, and organizations or users can change the applicable communication preferences.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID / Microsoft Entra admin center / PowerShell

2024-03-18.headline: Entra ID is moving Teams app consent to new resource-specific controls while retiring legacy RSC interfaces
2024-03-18.overview: The period’s only supplied item is a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice describing a service rollout and retirement, not a documentation clarification. Entra ID and Microsoft Teams are introducing teams- and chat-specific resource-specific consent settings for apps using Chat RSC and Team RSC. The notice does not identify the change as preview or generally available.
2024-03-18.adminImpact: The change began taking effect on March 7, 2024, with rollout to all tenants scheduled to complete by April 14, 2024. Administrators whose processes or tooling depend on the existing Group owner consent settings or API, or the existing Chat RSC API, need to account for their retirement. The new settings are managed through Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlets, and Teams-level administrators can manage them independently.

keyChanges.title: New consent controls apply to Teams and chat resources
keyChanges.detail: Resource-specific consent settings are being introduced for apps in Microsoft Teams, covering Chat RSC and Team RSC. Microsoft describes the change as intended to enhance secure app adoption, but supplies no further security requirements or configuration details.

keyChanges.title: Legacy consent settings and APIs are retiring
keyChanges.detail: The existing Group owner consent settings and API, together with the existing Chat RSC API, will be retired as part of this update. This creates a compatibility and administration impact for tenants or automation that still depend on those interfaces.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID — Group owner consent and Chat RSC

keyChanges.title: Administration shifts to Microsoft Graph PowerShell during a staged rollout
keyChanges.detail: The new teams-specific consent settings are managed using Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlets. Teams-level admins can manage them independently; the notice says the rollout started taking effect on March 7 and will be complete across tenants by April 14, 2024.

2024-04-29.headline: Dataverse user cleanup for Microsoft Entra identities enters public preview
2024-04-29.overview: The only supplied Entra-related change for the week is a Microsoft 365 Message Center announcement for a Microsoft Entra ID–related Dataverse capability. The feature is identified as a Public Preview launching 1 May 2024; it is not described as generally available or as a retirement.
2024-04-29.adminImpact: Administrators responsible for Dataverse environments may gain the ability to delete users in a disabled status, including delete stubs, unlicensed users, and users removed from Microsoft Entra groups. Microsoft cites privacy and regulatory requirements and storage reduction as the intended benefits. The evidence does not state that action is mandatory or provide rollout, configuration, eligibility, or automation details.

keyChanges.title: Public Preview of deleting disabled Dataverse users
keyChanges.detail: The announcement covers delete stubs, unlicensed users, and users removed from Microsoft Entra groups. Its summary describes the capability as deleting users with a disabled status from Dataverse environments. Microsoft positions this as a way to support privacy and regulatory obligations and free storage; no evidence is supplied about the deletion workflow or required administrator steps.

2024-05-13.headline: Week of 13 May: replace Workload ID symmetric keys by 15 June; passkey support begins rolling out
2024-05-13.overview: The supplied period contains two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices, with no documented Entra content additions, updates, or removals. The most consequential change is the planned disablement of symmetric keys for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals. Separately, Entra ID is beginning a staged authentication-strength improvement for device-stored passkeys.
2024-05-13.adminImpact: Organizations using symmetric keys for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals must replace them with asymmetric keys by 15 June 2024 to avoid authentication failures. No preparation is required for the Entra ID passkey rollout, although administrators may update relevant user documentation to reflect the new registration options.

keyChanges.title: Workload ID will disable symmetric keys for first-party application service principals
keyChanges.detail: This Microsoft 365 Message Center major update describes a security-driven authentication behavior change. Organizations must switch from symmetric to asymmetric keys by 15 June 2024; otherwise, affected authentication attempts may fail.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID authentication strength is being improved to support device-stored passkeys
keyChanges.detail: The rollout is scheduled to begin in mid-May 2024 and complete by early August 2024. Users will see new passkey registration options in My Security Info. The notice says no administrator preparation is needed; updating relevant documentation is optional.

2024-05-20.headline: Entra PIM is generally available for time-bound Dynamics 365 and Power Platform tenant admin roles
2024-05-20.overview: The week contained one Entra ID Message Center announcement. Microsoft announced general availability, beginning May 23, 2024, of managing admin roles for Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform through Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM). No documentation additions, updates, or removals were supplied.
2024-05-20.adminImpact: Administrators can use Microsoft Entra PIM to assign tenant admin roles for a defined period in Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform. The supplied announcement does not identify additional prerequisites, migration work, or configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: General availability of Entra PIM role management for Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform
keyChanges.detail: This is a general availability change—not a preview or documentation clarification. Beginning May 23, 2024, Microsoft Entra PIM supports assigning tenant admin roles for these workloads for a certain time period. The announcement was published in the Microsoft 365 Message Center on May 24.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID — Privileged Identity Management

2024-07-01.headline: Entra ID Conditional Access Insider Risk condition reaches general availability
2024-07-01.overview: The period’s sole substantive update is the general availability of Microsoft Entra’s Insider Risk condition in Conditional Access. The capability uses insider risk signals from Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection so organizations can enforce Conditional Access actions according to user risk levels. Rollout begins in early July 2024 and is expected to complete by early August 2024.
2024-07-01.adminImpact: Use of the capability requires an Entra ID P2 license and Adaptive Protection to be enabled. Eligible organizations can configure Conditional Access policies that respond to the resulting insider-risk signals; tenants may receive the capability during the stated rollout window.

keyChanges.title: Insider Risk condition is now generally available in Conditional Access
keyChanges.detail: This moves the condition from its prior status into general availability and adds insider-risk signals from Adaptive Protection as inputs for Conditional Access policy decisions. The available enforcement behavior is based on user risk levels, rather than only the existing Conditional Access conditions described in the evidence.

keyChanges.title: Prerequisites and rollout are explicit
keyChanges.detail: Organizations need both an Entra ID P2 license and enabled Adaptive Protection to use the feature. Microsoft’s message says rollout starts in early July 2024 and completes by early August 2024, so availability may arrive during that window rather than simultaneously for every tenant.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID / Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection

2024-07-08.headline: Azure AD Graph retirement is the clearest lifecycle signal in a sparse Entra week
2024-07-08.overview: The supplied period contains one Microsoft 365 Message Center item, posted 12 July, summarizing June 2024 Microsoft Entra updates. It flags Azure AD Graph retirement, Entra ID releases described as generally available, Apple-device security enhancements, and Entra ID updates affecting older Windows builds. No new, updated, or removed documentation items were supplied, and the record does not include the detail needed to establish feature names, dates, affected versions, or required actions.
2024-07-08.adminImpact: Azure AD Graph retirement is the most consequential item to validate in the underlying Message Center detail, but this record does not support a migration deadline or specific tenant action. The GA, Apple, and Windows references likewise lack enough detail to assess rollout, configuration, or compatibility impact. The period provides no evidence of an ordinary documentation clarification.

keyChanges.title: Azure AD Graph retirement called out
keyChanges.detail: The June 2024 roundup identifies Azure AD Graph Retirement. This is a capability-lifecycle change rather than a documentation update; the supplied message gives no retirement date, scope, migration guidance, or affected workload details.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD Graph

keyChanges.title: Entra ID general availability releases
keyChanges.detail: The message explicitly describes June releases for Entra ID as generally available. It does not name the releases, so no feature-level behavior, eligibility, or administrator step can be stated from the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: Security enhancements for Apple devices
keyChanges.detail: The roundup says that security enhancements for Apple devices were included. It does not identify the Apple platforms, controls, rollout behavior, or configuration changes, so their administrative impact cannot be determined.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID updates affecting older Windows builds
keyChanges.detail: The summary flags Entra ID updates affecting old Windows builds. No build numbers or description of the change are provided, so the evidence does not establish whether this is a support, compatibility, or behavior change.

2024-07-29.headline: Entitlement Management will prevent privileged administrators from bypassing access package approvals
2024-07-29.overview: Starting August 26, 2024, Entitlement Management will enforce access package policy approval settings for Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators. The supplied period contains a single Message Center notice describing this behavior change; it does not report a new feature launch, preview, retirement, or documentation update.
2024-07-29.adminImpact: No action is required from organizations because Microsoft says the change is automatic. Administrators should expect the affected privileged roles to be subject to the approval requirements configured in access package policies rather than being able to bypass them.

keyChanges.title: Approval enforcement extends to Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators
keyChanges.detail: Changes to Entitlement Management will prevent these two administrator roles from bypassing access package policy approvals. The change takes effect on August 26, 2024 and is described as an automatic update.

2024-08-05.headline: Week of 5 August 2024: Edge mobile Copilot retirement leads several Entra availability rollouts
2024-08-05.overview: The supplied period contains five Microsoft 365 Message Center announcements and no new, updated, or removed documentation items. The most consequential user-facing change is the retirement of Copilot in the Microsoft Edge mobile application for Entra ID users with version 128 in late August. Other substantive announcements move Attacker in the Middle detection in ID Protection, the AD FS application migration wizard, and device-based Conditional Access on Red Hat Enterprise Linux to general availability. A separate Dynamics 365 notice announces availability of a feature for deleting certain Microsoft Entra group users.
2024-08-05.adminImpact: The only explicit communication request is to inform affected users about the Edge mobile Copilot retirement and direct them to the Microsoft 365 mobile app for work or web chat. The ID Protection, AD FS migration wizard, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux Conditional Access announcements each state that no action is required before rollout. The Dynamics 365 notice confirms availability beginning 8 August but does not provide enough detail to infer a required cleanup, configuration change, or deletion workflow.

keyChanges.title: Retirement: Copilot in the Edge mobile application for Entra ID users
keyChanges.detail: Copilot in the Microsoft Edge mobile app will be retired with version 128 in late August 2024 for Entra ID users. No administrator action is required, but Microsoft recommends informing users and directing work users to the Microsoft 365 mobile app or web chat instead.

keyChanges.title: Generally available: Attacker in the Middle detection alert
keyChanges.detail: The Attacker in the Middle detection feature in Microsoft Entra ID Protection is scheduled to reach general availability by late August. The capability is intended to identify compromised user accounts, and the notice says no action is required before rollout.

keyChanges.title: Generally available: AD FS application migration wizard
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Entra ID AD FS application migration wizard provides a guided experience for migrating AD FS relying-party applications. Rollout begins in mid-August and is expected to complete by late August; no administrator action is required before the rollout.

keyChanges.title: Generally available: Device-based Conditional Access on Red Hat Enterprise Linux
keyChanges.detail: Device-based Conditional Access for Microsoft 365 and Azure resources on Red Hat Enterprise Linux is going generally available in mid-to-late August. The stated support includes Entra ID registration, Conditional Access policies, SSO, Intune compliance, and Red Hat RPM packages; no action is required before rollout.

keyChanges.title: Available: Dynamics 365 deletion of certain Microsoft Entra group users
keyChanges.detail: Starting 8 August 2024, Dynamics 365 will have a generally available feature to delete stub, unlicensed, and removed Microsoft Entra group users. The supplied announcement does not describe the trigger, scope, or administrator workflow, so it does not support a more specific operational recommendation.

2024-08-12.headline: Microsoft requires tenant MFA for admin-portal access by 15 October 2024
2024-08-12.overview: The week’s sole supplied change was a Microsoft 365 Message Center Major update for Entra ID Authentication. It is a security-enforcement notice, not a new feature or documentation clarification: tenants must enable MFA to retain administrative access to the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center.
2024-08-12.adminImpact: Administrators should enable MFA before 15 October 2024. The notice also identifies an option to apply to postpone the enforcement date if necessary; without MFA, administrative access to the listed portals will be restricted.

keyChanges.title: Tenant MFA deadline and access restriction announced
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft’s 16 August notice says MFA must be enabled for the tenant by 15 October 2024 for access to the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center. It advises setting up MFA early or applying to postpone enforcement where necessary. No other Entra feature, availability change, retirement, or documentation update is supplied for this period.

2024-09-02.headline: Microsoft Entra ID announces public preview of FIDO2 provisioning APIs
2024-09-02.overview: The period’s only supplied Entra change is a Microsoft 365 Message Center announcement for new FIDO2 provisioning APIs in public preview. The capability is intended to let organizations pre-provision security keys for users, simplifying onboarding and supporting phishing-resistant authentication. Rollout is scheduled to begin in mid-September 2024 and finish by late September.
2024-09-02.adminImpact: No administrator action is required for the rollout. The announcement does not provide configuration, eligibility, or migration requirements, and the capability should be treated as a public preview rather than a generally available feature.

keyChanges.title: Pre-provisioning of FIDO2 security keys enters public preview
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID is introducing APIs that enable security keys to be provisioned for users before onboarding. This changes the onboarding workflow the preview is designed to support, while the supplied notice does not establish general availability or require administrators to make changes during rollout.

2024-09-09.headline: Tenant MFA action deadline set for 15 October 2024
2024-09-09.overview: The week contains one Microsoft 365 Message Center action for Microsoft Entra ID. Administrators are asked to enable multifactor authentication (MFA) for the tenant by 15 October 2024 to access the Microsoft Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center. No supplied evidence indicates a new Entra feature, documentation change, or retirement during this period.
2024-09-09.adminImpact: Review tenant MFA readiness before the deadline. Postponement is possible, but administrators signing in without MFA will be prompted to register for it, which changes the sign-in experience and may affect access to the listed admin centers.

keyChanges.title: MFA becomes an explicit prerequisite for access to key admin centers
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center notice calls for tenant MFA enablement by 15 October 2024 for access to the Azure, Entra, and Intune admin centers. This is an administrative security action and deadline, not a product launch. If MFA is not enabled, admin sign-in will prompt MFA registration; the notice also states that postponement is available.

2024-10-07.headline: Microsoft Edge Mobile will change the New tab experience for Microsoft Entra ID users
2024-10-07.overview: The week contained one Microsoft 365 Message Center notice and no recorded Entra documentation additions, updates, or removals. The notice concerns Microsoft Edge Mobile rather than a new Entra ID capability: Wallpaper will be enabled by default on the New tab page, and a weather icon will be added. The changes were expected to roll out in early and late October 2024, respectively.
2024-10-07.adminImpact: No administrator action is required before the rollout. Administrators should expect affected Microsoft Entra ID users on Microsoft Edge Mobile to see the updated New tab defaults as the changes arrive.

keyChanges.title: Edge Mobile is changing the default New tab experience
keyChanges.detail: For Microsoft Entra ID users, Wallpaper will be enabled by default, with the wallpaper rollout expected in early October 2024. A weather icon was expected to follow in late October 2024. This is an announced user-experience behavior change, not evidence of a new Entra ID feature or a change to Entra ID administration.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Edge Mobile / Entra ID users

2024-10-14.headline: Entra message flags Azure AD Graph retirement, MFA enforcement and Apple-device security changes—but provides no operational details
2024-10-14.overview: The only supplied signal for the week of 14 October 2024 is a 15 October Microsoft 365 Message Center roundup for Microsoft Entra ID. Its summary says the September 2024 update covered general-availability releases, Azure AD Graph retirement, security enhancements for Apple devices and MFA enforcement. It is a communication pointing administrators to release notes, blog and email details—not a standalone record of a new feature, preview or documentation change made during this week.
2024-10-14.adminImpact: The message supports awareness but not a specific implementation step. The supplied evidence does not identify the affected GA releases, retirement date or migration scope, Apple-device behavior, MFA target population, enforcement schedule or prerequisites. Administrators need the referenced release material to determine whether action is required. No separate new, updated or removed documentation changes are recorded for the period.

keyChanges.detail: The summary says the update included MFA enforcement, but does not specify which users, tenants, authentication flows or policies are covered, nor when enforcement applies. No administrator action can be inferred from this message alone.

keyChanges.title: Security enhancements for Apple devices are called out
keyChanges.detail: The message identifies security work for Apple devices, but supplies no affected capability, platform behavior, rollout status or configuration requirement. The record therefore does not support a more specific assessment of impact.

keyChanges.title: General-availability releases are referenced but not identified
keyChanges.detail: The September roundup says it includes general-availability releases, but names no features or capabilities and provides no dates or availability scope. The reference alone is insufficient to characterize a launch or determine whether administrators need to change configuration.

2024-11-04.headline: Entra ID will reintroduce WhatsApp for MFA OTP delivery in India starting December 2024
2024-11-04.overview: The only supplied change for the week is a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update affecting Entra ID. Beginning in December 2024, users in India who have WhatsApp will receive MFA one-time passcodes through WhatsApp, with SMS used as a fallback. Microsoft says the channel will expand to additional countries, but does not specify which ones or when.
2024-11-04.adminImpact: Review whether WhatsApp-based OTP delivery fits the organization’s authentication policy before the rollout. Administrators can disable the feature or direct users toward stronger methods such as Microsoft Authenticator; the supplied notice does not provide configuration steps or a more specific rollout schedule.

keyChanges.title: WhatsApp becomes an MFA OTP delivery channel again
keyChanges.detail: This is a planned service behavior change and regional rollout—not a documentation-only clarification. Entra ID will reintroduce WhatsApp delivery in India from December 2024, with expansion to more countries. Users with WhatsApp will receive the code there, while SMS remains the fallback channel.

2025-01-20.headline: Entra ID is enabling Authenticator passkeys for FIDO2 organizations without key restrictions
2025-01-20.overview: The week of 20 January 2025 contains one substantive item: a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update for Entra ID Authentication. Starting in late January 2025, organizations with an enabled passkey (FIDO2) policy and no key restrictions will have passkeys available in the Microsoft Authenticator app. The supplied evidence describes an enablement notice, not a documentation change, and does not label the capability as preview or generally available.
2025-01-20.adminImpact: Administrators in the affected configuration should expect users to be able to add an Authenticator passkey through aka.ms/MySecurityInfo, with use enforced by Conditional Access policy. Organizations that do not want this enablement can impose key restrictions. No additional rollout scope or administrative steps are provided.

keyChanges.title: Authenticator passkeys become available under a specific FIDO2 policy configuration
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in late January 2025, passkeys in the Microsoft Authenticator app will be available to organizations that have enabled passkey (FIDO2) policy and have not configured key restrictions. Users can add the passkey through aka.ms/MySecurityInfo, and Conditional Access policy governs enforcement. This is the period’s only supplied change.

2025-02-17.headline: Entra is introducing a dedicated Viva Glint Tenant Administrator role
2025-02-17.overview: The week of 17 February contains one reported Entra change: a Microsoft 365 Message Center announcement about a new built-in role for Viva Glint. The rollout is expected from late March to early April 2025. No separate Entra documentation updates, retirements, or other product changes are included in the supplied period.
2025-02-17.adminImpact: The role is intended to let administrators manage Viva Glint settings without Global Administrator or User Administrator privileges. Administrators should review the role documentation, assess current role assignments, and communicate the change to affected staff before the rollout.

keyChanges.title: New built-in Viva Glint Tenant Administrator role
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is introducing the role in Microsoft Entra to provide Viva Glint settings management without requiring Global Administrator or User Administrator privileges. This is a planned rollout announcement, not evidence that the role is already generally available; the stated rollout window is late March to early April 2025.

2025-03-03.headline: Microsoft Entra rolls out a People administrator role while ID Protection alerts move to Defender XDR
2025-03-03.overview: The supplied record for the week of 3 March contains two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices and no documentation additions, updates, or removals. Microsoft Entra is rolling out a new People administrator role, while Entra ID Protection alerts are being removed from Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and integrated into Microsoft Defender XDR.
2025-03-03.adminImpact: The People administrator role is intended to support people-related administration and profile-photo management without requiring high privileges; the notice does not specify assignment steps or label the capability as preview or generally available. For ID Protection, the notice says no administrator action is required, but asks administrators to review their configuration and notify users about the change in alert location.

keyChanges.title: New People administrator role begins rollout
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra is introducing a People administrator role based on customer feedback. It allows management of people-related settings and profile photos without requiring high privileges. The stated rollout began in early February 2025 and is expected to complete by late March; the notice describes a rollout but does not establish preview or general-availability status.

keyChanges.title: ID Protection alerts leave Defender for Cloud Apps
keyChanges.detail: Starting 5 March 2025, Microsoft Entra ID Protection alerts are no longer available in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps and are integrated into Microsoft Defender XDR. This is a change to where the alerts are surfaced, not an evidence-based statement that ID Protection alerting itself is being retired. The notice says no admin action is required, while recommending configuration review and user notification.

2025-03-10.headline: Entra ID: “Require approved client app” control planned for retirement in March 2026
2025-03-10.overview: The only supplied update for the week is a Microsoft 365 Message Center reminder that the “Require approved client app” Conditional Access control will be retired in March 2026. Microsoft directs organizations to update affected policies to use the “Require application protection policy” grant control. This is a planned retirement notice, not a new feature, preview, general availability announcement, or evidence that the control has already been removed.
2025-03-10.adminImpact: Review Conditional Access policies that use the retiring control and plan updates to the named replacement before March 2026. The notice says rollout starts in late June 2026; tenants can keep or change the setting and should update user guidance. This is a changed authentication behavior, not a new authentication method.

keyChanges.title: Passkeys: new and revised operating guidance, with Windows explicitly in preview
keyChanges.detail: New and updated Microsoft Learn pages cover enabling, registering, and signing in with synced passkeys; Microsoft Authenticator on Android and iOS; FIDO2 security keys; and backup and restore when moving Authenticator to a new phone. The Windows-specific Entra passkey flow uses Windows Hello as a FIDO2 passkey provider and is labeled preview. A related External ID troubleshooting update warns that a phishing-resistant authentication-strength Conditional Access policy scoped to All resources can loop when a userAdds
keyChanges.product: Entra ID / External ID — Passkeys and Conditional Access

keyChanges.title: Authenticator passkey restore on iOS is scheduled for worldwide August availability
keyChanges.detail: Message Center describes a clearer, guided device-migration flow for restoring Microsoft Authenticator passkeys on iOS for users with iCloud backups. It will be available worldwide in August 2026, is enabled by default, and requires no administrator changes or action. This is a user-experience rollout, not a tenant configuration change.

keyChanges.title: General availability: Dynamics 365 Contact Center user management through Entra security groups
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft announced that managing Dynamics 365 Contact Center users through Microsoft Entra security groups will reach general availability on 24 July 2026. This is a GA milestone for that Contact Center integration; the supplied message does not state additional Entra configuration steps.
keyChanges.product: Entra ID — Security groups / Dynamics 365 Contact Center

2026-07-13.headline: Passkeys default in September; SMS/voice and SharePoint OTP retirements set Entra’s agenda
2026-07-13.overview: The period is dominated by two concrete authentication retirements and a related default change: Microsoft Entra says passkeys become the default on September 1, 2026, Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retire on February 1, 2027, and SharePoint One-Time Passcode authentication retires in October 2026 as external sharing transitions to Entra B2B. The other substantive thread is Microsoft Entra Internet Access and Global Secure Access Explicit Forward Proxy: this week’s Learn content documents PAC-based deployment and Entra/Conditional Access session controls, with HTTP-header session management marked preview. Microsoft also says Purview DLP network-layer filtering is targeted for general availability by September 2026. The remaining supplied Learn entries—RBAC and token reference, Lifecycle Workflows procedures, Netskope provisioning, Linux troubleshooting, and SLA data—are ordinary documentation maintenance; their summaries do not establish additional launches, behavior changes, or required configuration.
2026-07-13.adminImpact: Treat the authentication and external-sharing notices as the planning priorities. For SMS/voice, the Message Center notice says customers must configure telecom providers through the Microsoft Security Store or risk disruption; the companion Learn page focuses on migrating users to passkeys. For SharePoint, the notice says new external sharing has used Entra B2B since May 2026, external users need guest accounts, and admins should update policies and manage those accounts. For Explicit Forward Proxy deployments, the guidance says Conditional Access is not required but recommends restricting use to trusted networks and using Conditional Access to assign Internet Access security profiles; HTTP-header session management is preview. keyChanges.title: Passkeys become the default while Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retire
keyChanges.detail: This Entra ID change combines a behavior change with a retirement. Passkeys become the default authentication method on September 1, 2026, while Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retire on February 1, 2027. Customers using SMS or voice must configure telecom providers through the Microsoft Security Store or risk disruption. The notice describes passkeys as phishing-resistant and available at no extra cost; the new Learn page provides migration and preparation guidance.

keyChanges.title: SharePoint OTP transitions to Microsoft Entra B2B
keyChanges.detail: The External ID notice sets October 2026 as the retirement point for SharePoint One-Time Passcode authentication. It says new external sharing has used Microsoft Entra B2B since May 2026, and external users need guest accounts for access. The stated administrator preparation is to update policies and manage those guest accounts.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra External ID / Microsoft Entra B2B

keyChanges.title: Explicit Forward Proxy documentation broadens the deployment and security playbook
keyChanges.detail: The supplied Internet Access and Global Secure Access entries describe using Explicit Forward Proxy without the Global Secure Access client in PAC-capable browsers, hosting custom PAC files, delivering proxy and certificate-authority trust settings to Edge through Intune MAM, and using manual or DHCP/WPAD configuration for unmanaged devices. keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra Internet Access / Global Secure Access

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP integration receives a preview-to-GA timeline
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center item describes Microsoft Purview DLP integrating with Entra Global Secure Access Internet Access to filter sensitive files at the network layer and prevent leaks to unmanaged cloud apps. Its stated timeline places public preview in mid-November 2025 and general availability by September 2026. Administrators can create granular policies through Purview and Defender; the period’s notice is not evidence that general availability has already occurred.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra Internet Access / Global Secure Access

keyChanges.title: Admin control for SSO prompts is documented for managed Windows devices
keyChanges.detail: A new Entra ID Learn page says IT administrators can automatically accept SSO permissions on managed Windows devices through a supported registry setting. The supplied entry provides no rollout date or preview/GA status, so it should be treated as a newly documented control rather than a dated product-launch announcement.

2026-07-20.headline: Passkey GA and automatic FIDO2 migration lead the period, with network-layer DLP close behind
2026-07-20.overview: Authentication is the period’s main story, but the notices describe a mix of already-dated GA statuses and staged future rollouts rather than one July launch. Entra passkey profiles and synced passkeys are moving to GA for tenants with Passkeys (FIDO2) enabled, with existing configurations migrating through October. Windows passkeys are described as GA from late April, while passwordless password change is scheduled for late October and remains disabled by default. External ID documentation clarifies future SMS and voice retirement scope for B2B and internal guest users. Separately, Microsoft Purview DLP is rolling network-layer inspection and protection through Entra Internet Access (Global Secure Access) from July to October. The remaining Learn work is mostly maintenance or clarification; the new GSA egress-range and Databricks SCIM pages are operational references, not evidence of new service launches.
2026-07-20.adminImpact: Existing Passkeys (FIDO2) configurations and registration campaigns are subject to the stated regional migration. Windows passkeys are controlled through Authentication Methods policies and Conditional Access; the notice says no action is needed unless blocking is desired. The My Sign-Ins passwordless password-change capability remains off until an administrator activates it, while the SSPR CAPTCHA replacement requires no user or administrator action. The DLP rollout is cross-product, affecting Purview, Entra, and Defender administrators, but the supplied notice gives no specific configuration task. For External ID, the evidence establishes the affected user populations and planned passkey timing, not a retirement date or migration procedure. Learn updates are mostly documentation: the GSA

keyChanges.title: Passkey profiles and synced passkeys reach GA with automatic FIDO2-tenant migration
keyChanges.detail: The July 21 Message Center major update describes GA beginning in March 2026 for tenants with Passkeys (FIDO2) enabled. Existing configurations migrate to a Default passkey profile with a new `passkeyType` property, while automatic migration and registration-campaign changes roll out regionally through October 2026. Because the schedule is already underway, this is a GA and migration update rather than a new July launch.

keyChanges.title: Windows passkeys are GA; passwordless password change is a separate, later admin-enabled capability
keyChanges.detail: The Windows passkey notice places Entra passkeys on Windows in GA from late April 2026, without explicit opt-in, for corporate, personal, and shared devices. Authentication Methods policies and Conditional Access are the stated admin controls. Separately, passwordless users will be able to change passwords in My Sign-Ins with passkeys or Windows Hello, without the current password or SSPR; that capability is disabled by default, requires admin activation, and is scheduled for global rollout in late October 2026.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID — Windows passkeys and My Sign-Ins

keyChanges.title: Purview DLP is extending to the network layer through Entra Internet Access
keyChanges.detail: The major update describes Microsoft Purview DLP integrating with Entra Internet Access (Global Secure Access) to inspect and protect sensitive data at the network layer, including in AI interactions and cloud services. The stated capabilities include policy enforcement, alerts, and auditing, with rollout scheduled from July through October 2026. It explicitly affects Purview, Entra, and Defender administrators, but the supplied summary does not provide additional configuration steps.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra Internet Access (Global Secure Access) / Microsoft Purview DLP

keyChanges.title: External ID documentation clarifies SMS and voice retirement scope for B2B and internal guests
keyChanges.detail: An updated External ID page says B2B users and internal guest users are included in the retirement scope for Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication. It also says passkey support for those users is planned by the end of calendar year 2026. This is a future-scope clarification, not evidence that the retirement or passkey support completed during this period; no migration procedure or retirement date is supplied.

keyChanges.title: SSPR is replacing legacy CAPTCHA with backend abuse controls
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in early August 2026, Microsoft Entra self-service password reset is scheduled to replace its legacy CAPTCHA with backend throttling and behavior-based abuse detection. The notice says current password-reset functionality remains, no new controls are introduced, and neither users nor administrators need to act. This is a security and accessibility behavior change, not a new admin feature to configure.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID — Self-service password reset

2026-07-27.headline: Custom-branding CSS retirement and SMS/voice authentication phase-out lead the week
2026-07-27.overview: The week of 27 July 2026 is driven more by retirements, security guidance, and changed behavior than by a broad feature launch. Microsoft Entra ID has a Message Center retirement for custom CSS positioning in company branding beginning October 2026. Updated guidance prepares public-cloud tenants for the retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication and migration to passkeys. A separate Conditional Access notice describes stronger enforcement for certain narrow-scope sign-ins. Workload ID guidance moves GitHub Actions federated credentials toward immutable subjects. ID Governance also received substantial Tenant Governance guidance covering snapshots, configuration drift monitoring, related-tenant signals, and a Microsoft Graph preview; the supplied evidence does not establish a new GA launch for those documentation updates.
2026-07-27.adminImpact: Treat the branding and authentication items as planning work: identify custom CSS positioning properties, assess public-cloud users who still rely on Microsoft-provided SMS or voice authentication, and review GitHub Actions federated credentials that use mutable subjects. Evaluate custom applications requesting only the OIDC or directory scopes covered by the Conditional Access notice. If adopting Tenant Governance, review the application permissions and roles required for snapshots and monitors, and note that the Graph-related capability is marked preview. The passkey-registration optimization notice says organizations need no action; the other tenant-architecture, workflow, and setup changes are documentation guidance rather than confirmed service changes.

keyChanges.title: Custom branding CSS positioning properties retire in October 2026
keyChanges.detail: This Microsoft 365 Message Center major update affects Microsoft Entra ID company branding, not just documentation. Support for custom CSS positioning properties is scheduled to retire starting October 2026. Existing users must remove those properties; there is no migration path, and branding elements may remain visible but revert to default placement. Administrators should inventory affected branding configurations and plan their removal before the stated deadline.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication guidance shifts users toward passkeys
keyChanges.detail: An updated Microsoft Entra ID article explains how to prepare for retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication and migrate users to passkeys. The supplied timeline clarification applies to public cloud only; other cloud environments will follow later schedules with advance communications. keyChanges.title: Conditional Access enforcement changes for policies with resource exclusions
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center notice says that, starting June 15, 2026, Conditional Access policies targeting All resources with exclusions are enforced for sign-ins requesting only certain OIDC or directory scopes. Some users may encounter new challenges such as MFA. Most organizations need no action, but custom applications that request only the affected scopes should be evaluated. This is a changed-behavior notice, not a new Conditional Access feature launch.

keyChanges.title: GitHub Actions federated credentials should use immutable subjects
keyChanges.detail: New and updated Workload ID security guidance explains that mutable OIDC subject claims expose federated identity credentials to subject recycling, while immutable claims reduce that risk. For GitHub Actions, the guidance covers migrating to GitHub's immutable subject format and creating a separate credential for each subject a workflow presents, such as a branch or environment. Organizations using these credentials should review their current subject configuration; no migration deadline is supplied.

keyChanges.title: Tenant Governance documentation adds snapshots, drift monitoring, and related-tenant investigation
keyChanges.detail: New and updated ID Governance guidance now covers creating configuration snapshots for baselines or audit evidence, configuring monitors to evaluate a baseline and report drift, viewing monitor results, and assigning the service permissions and roles needed for those operations. Related-tenant guidance also explains how to use Microsoft Graph in preview to retrieve the users and applications behind tenant-discovery signals. These entries document an operational workflow and a preview API; they are not evidence of a

2026-08-03.headline: SMS/voice MFA retirement guidance sets September 2026 and February 2027 deadlines
2026-08-03.overview: The week was driven by documentation updates rather than newly announced releases: all five supplied changes were updates, with no new, removed, or Message Center items. The most consequential update is Entra ID guidance stating that passkeys will be automatically enabled for users using SMS or voice on September 1, 2026, followed by a February 1, 2027 restriction for tenants without a customer-managed telecom provider. The remaining updates refine provisioning extensibility, Global Secure Access Internet Access policy guidance, and licensing references.
2026-08-03.adminImpact: Prioritize a review of affected public-cloud users and their MFA transition plans. Administrators can move users out of SMS or voice policies before September 1, use the temporary opt-out while configuring a customer-managed provider, or migrate users to another method. The stated timeline excludes Azure AD B2C and Entra External ID. Provisioning, Internet Access, and licensing administrators should treat the other updates as configuration or reference work: evaluate the documented preview workflow, compare Internet Access policies and bypass rules with current settings, and validate licensing identifiers used by automation.

keyChanges.title: Entra ID guidance now states a two-stage SMS/voice MFA retirement timeline
keyChanges.detail: The updated retirement guidance says passkeys will be automatically enabled for users using SMS or voice on September 1, 2026. From February 1, 2027, tenants without a customer-managed telecom provider will no longer be able to use SMS or voice for MFA. The dates apply to public cloud; Azure AD B2C and Entra External ID are excluded. This is future behavior and transition guidance, not a report that the retirement occurred during this week.

keyChanges.title: Provisioning documentation adds a Graph implementation path for application attribute extensibility
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance explains how to create custom task extensions and extensibility workflows through Microsoft Graph, including required permissions and example requests and responses. It also describes linking the extension to an extensibility workflow and target attribute. The workflow example is labeled Preview, so the update should not be treated as a general-availability announcement. keyChanges.title: Internet Access guidance expands the documented Global Secure Access policy model
keyChanges.detail: The management article now describes traffic forwarding through the Global Secure Access client and remote networks, six policies instead of three, Microsoft Traffic Bypass, Custom Acquire, and Agentic Acquire. Custom Bypass instructions now cover destination types, ports, and protocols. This is a documentation and configuration-model update; the supplied evidence does not establish a separate availability or tenant-side behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Licensing reference data is refreshed for automation users
keyChanges.detail: The licensing reference is dated August 3, 2026, links to license management in the Azure portal, adds Agent 365, and revises service and plan identifier entries. Administrators using licensing APIs, PowerShell, or CSV data should check the updated identifiers. The change is to the reference material and does not state a change to licensing entitlements.

2023-09.headline: Entra ID announces a 30 September 2025 retirement deadline for legacy MFA and SSPR method management
2023-09.overview: September’s supplied record contains one consequential change: a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update issued on 29 September 2023. Microsoft says administrators will no longer be able to manage authentication methods through the legacy Multifactor Authentication (MFA) and Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) policies after 30 September 2025. This is a forward-looking retirement notice, not evidence of an immediate behavior change, new feature launch, preview, or general-availability milestone.
2023-09.adminImpact: Administrators should plan to move authentication methods managed in the legacy MFA and SSPR policies to Entra ID’s converged Authentication methods policy before the deadline. Microsoft describes the converged policy as the central management point for passwordless, multifactor authentication, and SSPR scenarios. The supplied notice does not provide migration steps or technical prerequisites, so more specific implementation guidance cannot be inferred.

keyChanges.title: Management is moving from separate legacy policies to the converged Authentication methods policy
keyChanges.detail: The announced retirement changes where authentication methods are managed: the legacy MFA and SSPR policies will lose that management capability on 30 September 2025, while Microsoft directs organizations to the converged Authentication methods policy for centralized management across passwordless, MFA, and SSPR scenarios.

2023-12.headline: Entra ID FIDO2 registration may now offer cross-device passkey creation
2023-12.overview: December’s substantive Entra change was a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice about the FIDO2 security key registration experience. During registration, users may see an operating system- or browser-generated prompt to create a passkey on another device, such as a phone or tablet; some users may instead see a QR code. The supplied evidence does not identify a preview or general-availability milestone, policy change, retirement, or required administrator action.
2023-12.adminImpact: The impact is primarily to the user and support experience. Administrators and support teams should recognize the cross-device passkey prompt or QR code as an expected possibility during FIDO2 registration. No configuration change, migration, or mandatory action is identified in the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: FIDO2 registration can present a cross-device passkey flow
keyChanges.detail: The registration experience may invoke a prompt generated by the operating system or browser to create a passkey on another device, including a phone or tablet. In some cases, a QR code facilitates that flow. This is a behavior change in registration—not evidence of a new policy, rollout milestone, or administrative requirement.

2024-01.headline: India-specific removal of WhatsApp-delivered MFA text messages was the only January Entra ID change
2024-01.overview: The supplied January 2024 data contains one Entra ID item: a 26 January Microsoft 365 Message Center notice about removing MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp in India. This is a service-change communication, not a new feature, preview, general-availability announcement, or documentation update. No new, updated, or removed Entra feature or documentation items were recorded.
2024-01.adminImpact: Organizations without users in India can safely disregard the notice. Organizations with users in India should determine whether they rely on this MFA delivery route. The supplied evidence does not provide an effective date, replacement method, or specific migration task, so no further action can be inferred.

keyChanges.title: Removal of MFA text message delivery via WhatsApp in India
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft 365 Message Center announced the removal of this India-specific authentication delivery route. Administrators with affected users should assess current reliance on it; the available evidence does not state when the removal takes effect or what replacement method is provided.

2024-02.headline: Entra ID plans a mid-March preview of device-bound passkeys, with FIDO2 policy and sign-in changes
2024-02.overview: February’s substantive Entra item is a Microsoft 365 Message Center notice, not a general-availability announcement or a documentation clarification. It says Microsoft Entra ID will begin preview support in mid-March 2024 for device-bound passkeys stored on computers and mobile devices, alongside existing FIDO2 security-key support. The change also introduces FIDO2 policy handling requirements and broadens end-user sign-in terminology.
2024-02.adminImpact: Administrators will need to enforce key restrictions in the FIDO2 policy to allow the passkey providers they intend to support. They should also expect the Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 sign-in option to be renamed and the sign-in experience to use broader passkey terminology. The notice does not state that existing FIDO2 security-key support is being retired or that migration is required.

keyChanges.title: Device-bound passkeys enter preview as an additional authentication method
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in mid-March 2024, Microsoft Entra ID is expected to support passkeys stored on computers and mobile devices in preview. This adds to, rather than replaces, the existing support for FIDO2 security keys; the supplied notice does not describe this as a general-availability release.

keyChanges.title: FIDO2 key restrictions will control permitted passkey providers
keyChanges.detail: The notice says administrators will need to enforce key restrictions in the FIDO2 policy to allow specified passkey providers. It does not identify the providers or provide additional policy parameters.

keyChanges.title: Windows Hello and FIDO2 sign-in wording becomes broader
keyChanges.detail: The end-user option for Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 security keys will be renamed to “Face, fingerprint, PIN, or security key.” The updated experience will also mention “passkey” so the terminology covers credentials presented from security keys, computers, and mobile devices.
keyChanges.product: Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 sign-in experience

2024-03.headline: March 2024: Entra consent administration shifts to new Teams controls and the Entra portal as legacy interfaces retire
2024-03.overview: March’s supplied Entra record consists of Microsoft 365 Message Center notices rather than documentation changes. The main operational theme is consent control migration: Teams and chat resource-specific consent settings are rolling out while legacy Group owner and Chat RSC interfaces retire, and the tenant-wide user-consent setting is leaving the Microsoft 365 admin center for the Entra portal. The other notices cover Entra PIM in public preview in the Power Platform admin center and changed Copilot welcome-email behavior for licenses assigned through PowerShell or the Entra admin center.
2024-03.adminImpact: Use the Entra portal for tenant-wide user-consent policy after the Microsoft 365 admin-center retirement; existing settings remain unchanged and no preparation is required for that transition. Teams administrators or automation that depend on the retiring consent settings or APIs should account for the new Microsoft Graph PowerShell-managed settings as rollout reaches all tenants by April 14. Treat the Power Platform PIM capability as preview. If Copilot licenses are assigned outside the Microsoft 365 admin center, organizations can adjust direct-communication preferences there, while individual users can change their own settings through security and privacy controls.

keyChanges.title: Teams and chat app consent gets new resource-specific controls
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Teams are introducing teams- and chat-specific consent settings for Team RSC and Chat RSC. The existing Group owner consent settings and API, along with the existing Chat RSC API, will be retired. The new settings are managed with Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlets, and Teams-level administrators can manage them independently. The rollout began taking effect on March 7 and is scheduled to reach all tenants by April 14. The notice describes a staged service change, not a preview or a
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Teams

keyChanges.title: Microsoft 365 admin-center user-consent control retires
keyChanges.detail: The User consent to Apps setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center will be retired in early April. This changes the administration surface rather than the policy itself: existing settings remain unchanged, but administrators will no longer be able to edit the tenant-wide policy there. The Entra portal is the replacement location, and the notice says no preparation is required.

keyChanges.title: Entra PIM is in public preview in the Power Platform admin center
keyChanges.detail: The March notice announces public preview of Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management in the Power Platform admin center, while noting that the capability was already available there on February 5. It brings Entra PIM’s ability to manage, control, and monitor access into that administrative context. This is a preview announcement, not evidence of general availability or a new March launch.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID and Power Platform admin center

keyChanges.title: Copilot welcome emails extend to licenses assigned outside the Microsoft 365 admin center
keyChanges.detail: During a late-March through late-April rollout, end users assigned Copilot for Microsoft 365 licenses through PowerShell or the Microsoft Entra admin center will automatically receive a welcome email when direct communications from Microsoft are enabled. Organizations can change communication preferences in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and individuals can change their own through security and privacy settings. This is a change in email behavior, not a reported licensing or provisioning migration.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID and Copilot for Microsoft 365

2024-05.headline: May 2024: Workload ID key disablement creates an urgent June deadline, alongside passkey, PIM, and Dataverse changes
2024-05.overview: The supplied May record is announcement-led: four Microsoft 365 Message Center notices, with no supplied documentation additions, updates, or removals. The most consequential change is the required replacement of symmetric keys for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals. Other notices cover a staged passkey-related behavior improvement, general availability of Entra PIM role management for Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform, and a Dataverse cleanup capability entering public preview.
2024-05.adminImpact: Organizations using symmetric keys for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals must replace them with asymmetric keys by June 15, 2024, or risk authentication failures. No preparation is required for the passkey rollout, although relevant user documentation may need updating. PIM is available for time-bounded tenant admin roles, while the Dataverse cleanup capability is preview functionality and is not described as mandatory.

keyChanges.title: Symmetric keys for first-party service principals will be disabled
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft announced a security-related behavior change for Microsoft Entra first-party application service principals. Organizations must switch from symmetric to asymmetric keys by June 15, 2024, to avoid authentication failures.

keyChanges.title: Authentication-strength improvements begin supporting device-stored passkeys
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra ID is rolling out new authentication-strength support for passkeys stored on devices. Users will see additional registration options in My Security Info as the rollout proceeds from mid-May through early August 2024. No preparation is required, though administrators may update relevant documentation.

keyChanges.title: Entra PIM role management for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform reaches general availability
keyChanges.detail: Beginning May 23, administrators can use Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management to assign Dynamics 365 Apps and Power Platform tenant admin roles for a defined period. The announcement does not identify additional prerequisites, migration work, or configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: Dataverse user cleanup enters public preview
keyChanges.detail: Beginning May 1, the preview provides the ability to delete disabled-status users from Dataverse environments, including delete stubs, unlicensed users, and users removed from Microsoft Entra groups. Microsoft cites privacy and regulatory requirements and storage reduction as intended benefits; the supplied evidence does not make deletion mandatory or specify eligibility and configuration details.

2024-07.headline: Insider Risk in Conditional Access reaches GA; Entitlement Management will enforce approvals for privileged administrators
2024-07.overview: July’s supplied record is sparse and message-center-led, with no new, updated, or removed documentation items. Its clearest capability change is the general availability of the Insider Risk condition in Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, using Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection signals. The supplied July 29 brief also reports an automatic Entitlement Management behavior change effective August 26. A July roundup flags Azure AD Graph retirement and Apple/older-Windows updates, but does not provide enough detail for migration or compatibility guidance.
2024-07.adminImpact: Organizations need an Entra ID P2 license and Adaptive Protection enabled to use the Insider Risk condition; eligible tenants can configure policies as rollout proceeds from early July through early August 2024. The Entitlement Management change requires no preparation according to the supplied notice, but Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators should expect configured access-package approval requirements to apply to them. The Azure AD Graph reference supports follow-up validation, not a specific deadline or migration action.

keyChanges.title: Insider Risk condition in Conditional Access reaches general availability
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access can use insider-risk signals from Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection to enforce policy actions according to user risk levels. This is a generally available capability, not a preview. Use requires Adaptive Protection and an Entra ID P2 license, with rollout stated to begin in early July 2024 and complete by early August 2024.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access / Microsoft Purview Adaptive Protection

keyChanges.title: Entitlement Management will stop privileged-role bypass of access-package approvals
keyChanges.detail: Starting August 26, 2024, the supplied notice says access package policy approval settings will be enforced for Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators. This is a behavior change: those roles will no longer bypass configured approval requirements. The notice says the change is automatic and requires no organizational action.

keyChanges.title: Azure AD Graph retirement is flagged without migration detail
keyChanges.detail: The July 12 “What’s new in Microsoft Entra – June 2024” message names Azure AD Graph retirement and also mentions unspecified GA releases, Apple-device security enhancements, and changes affecting older Windows builds. It provides no retirement date, affected versions, feature names, or required action, so these references should be treated as lifecycle signals rather than a complete migration or compatibility advisory.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD Graph

2024-08.headline: Tenant MFA deadline leads August: privileged approval bypass ends and Edge mobile Copilot retires
2024-08.overview: August’s supplied Entra record is operational rather than documentation-led: all seven entries are Microsoft 365 Message Center notices, with no new, updated, or removed documentation items. The highest-impact item is the requirement to enable tenant MFA by 15 October 2024 to preserve access to three admin centers. Two other behavior changes affect users and privileged administrators: Copilot in Edge mobile retires for Entra ID users with version 128 in late August, and Entitlement Management will enforce access-package approvals for Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators from 26 August. The remaining substantive notices are general-availability rollouts for ID Protection detection, AD FS application migration, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux device-based Conditional Access.
2024-08.adminImpact: Enable MFA before 15 October, or use the stated postponement option if necessary; without it, access to the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center will be restricted. No pre-rollout action is stated for the general-availability notices or the automatic Entitlement Management change, but administrators should expect configured access-package approval requirements to apply to the two named privileged roles. For the Edge retirement, Microsoft recommends informing users and pointing them to the Microsoft 365 mobile app for work or web chat. The separate Dynamics 365 deletion notice confirms availability but provides too little detail to support a cleanup or configuration recommendation.

keyChanges.title: Tenant MFA is required for admin-portal access by 15 October
keyChanges.detail: This is security-enforcement guidance, not a new capability: tenants must enable MFA by 15 October 2024 to access the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Intune admin center. The notice says tenants may set up MFA early or apply to postpone enforcement; without MFA, administrative access will be restricted.

keyChanges.title: Entitlement Management removes privileged-administrator approval bypass
keyChanges.detail: This behavior change takes effect on 26 August 2024: Global Administrators and Identity Governance Administrators can no longer bypass the approval settings configured in access package policies. Microsoft describes the update as automatic and says no organizational action is needed.

keyChanges.title: Copilot in Edge mobile is retired for Entra ID users
keyChanges.detail: This is a retirement, not a rollout: Copilot leaves the Microsoft Edge mobile application for Entra ID users with version 128 in late August 2024. 2026-01.headline: January 2026: two Entra authentication retirements outweigh a month of documentation maintenance
2026-01.overview: January’s consequential administrator work is deadline-driven rather than a feature-release cycle. The record contains 299 changes—292 updates, one new page, three removals, and three Message Center notices. The notices announce the retirement of Conditional Access’s “Require approved client app” control in June 2026 and custom greetings for voice-call MFA on February 28, 2026. Microsoft Purview DLP also renamed its Enforcement plane from “Entra” to “Application,” without functional or user impact. The supplied evidence establishes no new preview or general-availability release. The sole new page is an EcoOnline Info Exchange SSO configuration tutorial, not evidence of a new Entra capability; the three removed Purview workload-content pages have no stated retirement rationale.
2026-01.adminImpact: Inventory Conditional Access policies that use “Require approved client app” and plan migration to “Require application protection policy” before the June retirement. Prepare voice-MFA users for Microsoft’s default recordings and review relevant configurations before February 28. Update Purview DLP scripts and internal documentation to recognize “Application” in new audit logs while retaining “Entra” for existing logs. For deployments in scope, review the revised Conditional Access Optimization Agent, ID Protection, Microsoft Entra Connect Sync, and External ID/Akamai WAF guidance. The evidence supports targeted runbook checks, not a blanket tenant reconfiguration.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access will retire the “Require approved client app” control
keyChanges.detail: Retirement notice: Microsoft says the control will retire in June 2026 and will no longer be enforceable afterward. Administrators should identify policies using the old control and update them ahead of the retirement.

keyChanges.title: Custom voice-MFA greetings will be replaced by default recordings
keyChanges.detail: Retirement notice: custom greetings in voice-call authentication end on February 28, 2026. Voice MFA calls will use Microsoft’s default recordings after that date. keyChanges.title: Purview DLP’s Enforcement plane label changes from “Entra” to “Application”
keyChanges.detail: Naming clarification: Microsoft Purview DLP began renaming the Enforcement plane in mid-January. There is no stated functional, user, or compliance impact. New audit logs use “Application,” while existing logs retain “Entra,” so scripts and documentation that depend on the label may need updating.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access Optimization Agent guidance documents an activator-identity distinction
keyChanges.detail: A coordinated update to five Entra Conditional Access Optimization Agent pages records that agents enabled after November 17, 2025 no longer use the identity of the user who activated them. Earlier agents may fail when the activating account relied on Privileged Identity Management but lacked the required permissions when the agent ran. This is operational documentation and troubleshooting guidance; it does not establish a preview, general-availability event, or January-wide rollout.
